storySection.title: Bringing Color to Life with AR & Immersive Tech
paragraphs: At Prakria, we are always stretching the limits of what brand experiences can be. With Con Vida, a sketch pen brand from our proof-of-concept slate, we set out to illustrate the intersection of different realms of color, technology, and creative imagination. The goal: to take a static pack full of color and bring it to life in an innovative way through new media forms like AR, VR, animation, and playful, interactive storytelling.

While Con Vida was artificial in the sense that it was not a real market launch, it was an experimental playground. We wanted to demonstrate that packaging could be more than just a wrapper; it could be a portal to fully immersive realities. The balancing act was engaging the audience in a magical way that required the combination of augmented reality app development, animated video development, virtual reality development, and interactive tech, all in a small, delightful experience.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: With Con Vida, Prakria set out to prove that even something as simple as a pack of sketch pens can be turned into a living experience where design, technology, and storytelling leap off the packaging.

list.text: The main task at hand was to transform a flat, static product into an interactive world of color and motion, using AR, VR, and animation as storytelling tools rather than novelties.
We needed to show how packaging can be a portal, not just a container, to a playful and immersive brand experience.
It was a balancing act of creativity and technology: it had to feel magical and delightful, but needed to be lightweight, stable, and performant on mobile.

As proof of concept, Con Vida needed to demonstrate the studio's ability in fusing AR/VR development, animation, and game-thinking together into a cohesive whole—the making of not a tech demo, but a living, breathing story.
The goal was to create a small, self-contained experience that captures imagination, showing Prakria's creative technology capabilities to future clients.
The challenge was to paint beyond the page, to prove that through AR and animation, color could transcend packaging and live in the user's world.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: The Con Vida project turned packaging into a living, interactive portal by merging AR, animation, and VR-ready frameworks. The focus was on demonstrating how color could move, breathe, and interact with users through their devices.

list.title: Packaging as Portal
list.description: Initially, we developed a fresh, playful package for Con Vida—something you could see before you engaged with the tech layer. Then we translated it to a 3D model environment (although AR implies). This way, it would work well with the augmented overlay and animation.

list.title: AR Activation
list.description: Users would just use the app to scan the pack and then the magic happens: colors come to life from the packaging, drawings animate, and the design is now a living frame. We created this as an augmented reality app development exercise, a pack-to-screen translation of brand personality.

list.title: Animation & Motion
list.description:
To animate that burst, we incorporated animated video creation techniques in the AR layer: playful flows of color, sketch lines moving, petals and pigments dancing in space. In effect, the physical pack becomes an animation stage.

In the best expansion scenarios we'd examined, we also mapped how game development or mobile game development elements could fit into this world—for example, to enable users to 'paint' virtual illustrations, or unlock layers of augmentations. Here's where game development services think edge in: interactive experience, more than just passive viewing.

list.title: VR & Beyond
list.description: Although Con Vida's proof of concept focused on AR, the underlying architecture we developed could also be used to extend to either virtual reality development or completely immersive VR development experiences. The same assets could also be used as portals within the headsets to literally let the user step inside the colored world. We also foresaw a future development path for AR/VR, or AR/VR app development, that develops this concept into richer ways.

executionSection.title: THE CREATIVE EXECUTION
executionSection.description: We created the AR pack experience for scanning layers to animate or react in animated layers, particle effects, or motion graphics, all designed to be fun and magical.

list.title: Lightweight, Expressive Animation
list.description: The AR animations were designed to be expressive yet lightweight — generating and tracking seamlessly on mobile devices. Their frame counts were purposely optimized to retain magical impact while ensuring fast performance even on modest hardware.

list.title: Modular & Extensible Structure
list.description: We built the system on a modular architecture, enabling new features — like mini games, drawing tools, or even VR environments — to be added as additional layers without needing to rebuild the core experience.

list.title: Mapped Evolution Routes
list.description: Extension scenarios were mapped from the start, exploring how the project could eventually grow: new mobile game modes, expanded user interactions, or full VR spin-offs for deeper immersion.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: Despite Con Vida being a concept rather than an actual product, it delivered on its mission superbly:

list.text: It became an exemplar of what animated video creation + AR + design can do.
It demonstrated how packaging can surpass its physical limitations and serve as a conduit for experience.
It established Prakria as a team that is looking forward to handling game dev services, AR/VR dev, and immersive app work—not only static design.
For clients considering our capabilities, Con Vida makes the conversation easy: “What if your product could be animated?”

whySection.title: WHY THIS MATTERS
whySection.description: Con Vida is evidence that packaging does not need to remain on the shelf; it can leap into your phone, your space, your imagination.

list.title: Why AR?
list.text: Augmented reality app development is justified when it meaningfully changes the way people view a product.

list.title: Movement & Life
list.text: Backing this up with animated video creation adds movement and life to what would otherwise be flat.

list.alt: VR and Game Dev Expansion icon
list.title: Layering Experiences
list.text: Looking ahead, you can layer in game development, VR development, and full AR VR app development to enhance the experience.

list.title: Elevated Storytelling
list.text: A proof of concept like this shows how game development services and immersive tech can provide an elevated storytelling experience to a brand.

storySection.title: When Holiday Cheer Meets Augmented Magic
paragraphs: As December arrived, Polo wanted to go beyond traditional social media campaigns. Instead of static visuals, they sought an interactive and shareable experience — one that would encapsulate the joy and sparkle of the holiday season.

The concept was to develop a Christmas AR filter that users could interact with, record, and share across platforms. The challenge was to keep it festive, branded, and delightful while ensuring smooth, intuitive performance across devices — a joyful experience without friction.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: Polo wanted to do more than just static festive campaigns; it wanted to create an interactive, shareable AR experience that really spread the holiday joy with the same freshness and fun the brand is known for.

list.text: The task was to design an AR experience that blended holiday spirit with brand personality, without feeling gimmicky or overproduced.
It had to be a technically polished but lightweight filter, working flawlessly on a wide variety of mobile phones and social platforms.
It had to be intuitive and delightful, instantly recognizable as Polo, yet universally enjoyable to users celebrating the season.
Every visual and animation element needed to hit the right balance of: Christmassy, branded, fun while retaining real-time performance.
The deeper challenge was making sure the filter didn't just entertain but invited participation, creating and sharing one's own festive moments with Polo at the center.

challenge.conclusionLine: The task, in short, was to change a humble social filter into a magical branded experience-one that spread Polo's festive cheer through interaction, not advertising.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: We created a filter where users see themselves surrounded with Polo Christmas elements (like sparkly candy canes, falling snow, animated lights, and Polo mints decorated with festive touches in between), all triggered by face detection and anchored around the user in AR.

list.title: Created the core AR experience
list.description: We used AR development techniques, so filters felt organic on the user’s face and around.

list.title: Added 2D/3D animation elements
list.description: Animations of snow, sparkly lines, and holiday icons dancing around the user’s head.

list.title: Added motion and visual effects
list.description: This animated things up — snow drift, glowing pulse, light trails — to help create a polished feeling of animation.

list.title: Created an implementation
list.description: Assured the filter experience was performant across mobile devices, with little to no lag time, and visual fidelity.

startageySection.conclusionLine: Since filters are “always on screen”, each animation decision is light, festive, and non-intrusive - to provide delight, when possible, without interruption.

executionSection.title: THE CREATIVE EXECUTION
executionSection.description: After the AR filter was developed, it was launched via social channels (Instagram, Snapchat) and branded channels. Users could:

list.description: Try it live, and capture short videos of themselves in the Polo AR festive world.
Take still-image shots with the animated filter overlays.
Share directly to stories, messages, and social media etc.

executionSection.conclusionLine: We also created teaser animations, a promotional banner image, and AR previews to support Polo with the promotion of the filter across both its digital and physical channels.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The Polo Christmas AR Filter turned into an asset that was shared publicly - people were using it for celebratory content, holiday greetings, and social posts.

list.text: This helped brand engagement: users did not just see Polo messaging, but rather experienced it in their own context.
The animation and festive layer raised the bar with Polo’s seasonal campaign to be more than just a standard visual asset.
The overall performance and polish of the filter demonstrated our capabilities in augmented reality application development and AR + animation execution.

whySection.title: WHY THIS MATTERS
whySection.description: The AR filter represents more than a leap in holiday fun; it demonstrates how brands can today:

list.text: Utilise augmented reality development to bring packaging or branding into the consumer spaces of users.
Mix animated video creation with motion and AR to evoke an emotional connection.
Realise that AR VR app development and the essence of AR VR development thinking can be applied to even a lightweight social experience.
Think of filters and immersive technology not just as novelties, but as strategic extensions to the brand.

whySection.conclusionLine: As an animation / AR / VR studio, Prakria sees every filter as a connection between a brand and a user, a magical moment, and a chance to put some delight into someone’s day

storySection.title: Blending Storytelling, Technology & Imagination
paragraphs: Prakria was changing: it was more than just visuals — we were hoping to be a full creaTech studio, integrating creative capability with modern technology like AR & VR.
To show we could change like that, we decided to develop engaging Proof of Concepts. One of the first was a concept wine brand called Blanca Wine, created in Spanish vineyards.

The brief was quite ambitious: start a brand (narrative, visuals, pack), then bring it to life with immersive technologies. The goal was to create an experience, not just static images, where you could step into the wine story. That’s where AR, animation, and interactive technology would play a featured role.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: Blanca Wine wasn't a client brief; it was a creative experiment. Prakria set out to prove that a brand could live not just on shelves but in stories, screens, and immersive spaces.

list.text: The ambition was to create a complete brand from scratch—identity, narrative, visuals, packaging—and then reimagine it through immersive technologies like AR and VR.
The concept had to merge storytelling with technology in such a way that users wouldn't just see the wine; they'd experience it.
The team had to design every layer of reality: a 3D bottle, augmented vineyard, and interactive storytelling—all working seamlessly across devices.
The project needed to demonstrate technical prowess—AR/VR/app development—but feel elegant, emotive, and human rather than a tech demo in and of itself.

As proof of concept, Blanca had to showcase what the future of brand storytelling looks and feels like, how creative technology can turn something as humble as packaging into a digital doorway of emotion and experience.

challenge.conclusionLine: The challenge was to transform a conceptual wine brand into a real one, living and breathing, proof that technology and storytelling can fuse as beautifully as the wine itself

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: We started with the brand narrative — its history, its ethos, its visual tone, and communication scaffolding. Then, we designed the wine bottle in 3D, creating both literal and virtual versions enriched through AR and animation.

list.title: Brand Identity & 3D Design
list.description: We started with the brand narrative — its history, its ethos, its visual tone, and its communication scaffolding. Then, we began building the wine bottle in a 3D model — designing its shape and materials, label and reflections, and cap in a detailed, small form so it could live in literal form or virtual form.

list.title: AR Experience & Immersion
list.description:
In order to create an experience with Blanca, we developed an augmented reality experience where you can scan the bottle or its packaging, and it unlocks an experience in a vineyard in Spain with lots of light. You can see how the vines move with the light and feel the wind moving by, all in an AR experience.

The ability to create such an immersive journey was possible because of AR VR app development techniques, which allow us to combine an AR scene with spatial anchoring, so it seamlessly fits into your environment.

list.title: Animation & Motion
list.description:
In order to enhance the AR storytelling, we incorporated animated video creation within the experience: vine leaves flutter, birds fly overhead, wine is poured into a glass... motions that will contribute to the sense of immersion.

We also considered optional extensions like game design or mobile game development modules as in, imagine mini-AR games to "harvest grapes" or "blend wine" and to engage people with gameplay and brand content. That's where thinking of game development services intersects with branded experiences.

list.title: VR / Future Escapes
list.description: Although Blanca mainly resides in AR today, the foundation is ready for virtual reality development or full VR development experiences — walking through cellars, tasting rooms, a vineyard tour, etc. This same digital bottle, narrative and environment can extend into that space within an AR VR development or both AR/VR app development pipelines.

executionSection.title: THE CREATIVE EXECUTION
executionSection.description: A sleek, high-fidelity 3D model of the Blanca wine bottle for rendering and AR overlay

list.description: AR filter/experience layers bringing the visual narrative to users’ screens
Animated scenes woven into AR to create motion, depth, and storytelling
Modular structure, so additional layers like mini-games or VR tours could be added without reworking the core

executionSection.conclusionLine: Assets ready for social sharing, internal demos, and brand engagement

resultSection.title: THE RESULT
resultSection.description: The Blanca Proof of Concept became more than a showcase -it became a conversation starter:

list.text: It demonstrated how animated video creation, AR, and 3D modeling can elevate even a conceptual brand.
It showed clients that packaging can be a portal, not just a wrapper. A bottle becomes an experience.
It highlighted Prakria’s ability in AR VR app development, VR development, and immersive storytelling, not just design.

resultSection.conclusionLine: Because Blanca was designed as a proof project, it let us experiment, iterate, and push boundaries without constraints.

whySection.title: WHY THIS MATTERS
whySection.description: Blanca proves that brands can be more than visual, they can be immersive, interactive, and emotionally resonant.

list.text: AR / VR technologies are not tricks -when implemented with care, they enrich brand storytelling.
